title: Three synchronous cross-process ledger transactions per completion; contention blocks the loop 15s
evidence: llm.py:2651 (`self.budget.check()` pre-dispatch), 2714-2715 (`record()` then `check()` post) — each takes `_exclusive_ledger_lock` (llm.py:1196-1274) which opens/locks a lock file and, when contended, loops `time.sleep(0.02)` synchronously (llm.py:1226, 1245, 1258) for up to `_LEDGER_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S=15` (llm.py:142); `_load_ledger` reads and `_save_ledger` atomically rewrites JSON on every `record` (llm.py:1299-1317, 1415-1426). Each failed OpenRouter retry attempt adds another full transaction (llm.py:2453-2458). All on the asyncio thread.
win_rate_impact: Every LLM call pays 3 file-lock + disk round-trips on the hot path; when a second SkyN3t process (dashboard/status or a concurrent build sharing data_dir) holds the lock, each transaction blocks the WHOLE event loop in a synchronous sleep-poll for up to 15s — three times per completion — stalling all parallel slices and stream watchdogs. Under fan-out this converts bookkeeping into serialized dead time that eats build windows.
fix: Coalesce the pre-check with the post-record check (one guarded transaction per call), skip the disk read in `check()` when the ledger was loaded within the last few seconds, and run the ledger transaction in `asyncio.to_thread` (or make the poll `await asyncio.sleep`) so contention never blocks the loop.

title: _openrouter builds a fresh httpx.AsyncClient (new TCP+TLS handshake) for every attempt
evidence: llm.py:4492-4495 — `async with (provider_slot(...), httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=request_timeout) as client:)` inside `_do`, which runs once per attempt per candidate. Dozens of small completions per build (brainstorm/critic/reviewer/intent/test_author call sites across skyn3t/agents and skyn3t/studio) each pay connection setup; retries and failover multiply it. The agentic loop already demonstrates the right pattern (one client for the whole session, llm.py:3301).
win_rate_impact: Adds a TLS handshake (~100-300ms plus loop work) to every completion attempt and forfeits connection reuse across the build's many small scoring/review calls — seconds to minutes of aggregate wall clock per build under fan-out, spent on connection churn that buys zero success probability and widens the window in which stage deadlines expire.
fix: Hold one shared `httpx.AsyncClient` per event loop (same keyed-by-loop pattern as provider_limits._ADMISSIONS), pass the per-request timeout via `client.post(..., timeout=...)`, and close it on loop teardown.

title: Embedder backend drift silently makes the persisted vector store unreachable
evidence: Embedder picks sentence-transformers (dim 384) vs hashing fallback (dim 256) per-process at import/first-use, and degrades to hashing mid-run on any model-load or encode failure (embeddings.py:60, 69-76, 114-115) — e.g. a blocked HuggingFace download. A chroma collection persisted under one dimension then rejects queries/upserts of the other; vector_store.query catches the exception and scores only the in-memory _docs (vector_store.py:214-234), which are empty after restart — so recall returns [] with only a log warning. semantic_skills._cosine likewise returns 0.0 on length mismatch (semantic_skills.py:30-31).
win_rate_impact: Everything the factory persisted across sessions (build experience, ingested GitHub repos via `domain ingest`) silently vanishes from recall whenever the embedding backend differs from the one that wrote the store — a one-time network hiccup at ST model load permanently orphans the entire knowledge base for that process with no operator-visible signal, degrading codegen context on every subsequent build.
fix: Persist a {backend, dim} marker beside the collection (or encode it in the collection name, e.g. skyn3t_rag_st384 / skyn3t_rag_hash256) and have VectorStore/Embedder pin to the store's recorded backend at startup, logging loudly (or surfacing via info()) when the preferred backend is unavailable.

title: Dead event stream freezes all live status; only a 2px sidebar dot changes
evidence: Stream status is rendered solely as a small dot/label at the sidebar bottom (App.jsx:86-91, 139-154). No consumer of the stream inspects stream.status: GateLadder (GateLadder.jsx:131-134), Studio's pipeline/StageLedger (Studio.jsx:1013-1016), and Projects' useServedMap (Projects.jsx:104-126) keep rendering the last-received events unchanged when status is 'closed'/'error', with 'forging'/'running' animations still pulsing.
win_rate_impact: When the server restarts or the socket drops mid-build, the operator watches a frozen cockpit that still claims stages are igniting and previews are live - they wait out builds that already finished or failed, and events emitted during the gap beyond the 50-frame prime are silently lost with no staleness cue.
fix: Thread stream.status into the live panels: when status !== 'open', overlay a 'stream disconnected - data stale since <time of last frame>' banner on GateLadder/Forge line/Stage ledger and pause the running animations.

title: Model-catalog 'refresh' button never sends refresh=true - routing pins use stale pricing
evidence: The catalog queryFn serializes `refresh: catalogRefreshing` (Studio.jsx:687-692) but catalogRefreshing is not in the queryKey (Studio.jsx:678-685), and the click handler calls setCatalogRefreshing(true) then catalog.refetch() synchronously (Studio.jsx:1528-1534) - refetch executes the closure from the current render where catalogRefreshing is still false, so the request always goes out as refresh=false (backend force_refresh gate at routes.py:7206). The button label also keys off catalog.isLoading, which stays false during a refetch, so no 'refreshing' feedback appears.
win_rate_impact: The operator pins codegen/tier models and reads example costs from a cached OpenRouter catalog that the refresh control silently fails to update - stale prices and delisted/renamed models get pinned, producing routing failures or unexpected paid routes on subsequent builds.
fix: Track a refresh nonce in state, include it in the queryKey, and have the queryFn send refresh=true when the nonce changed (resetting after success); switch the button label to catalog.isFetching.

title: Studio vision fn bills the paid default model under free_only, outside the budget ledger
evidence: visual_check.py:477-502 (_make_openrouter_vision_fn) picks model = settings.vision_model or _DEFAULT_VISION_MODEL ("openai/gpt-4o-mini", visual_check.py:37 — paid) and POSTs directly via httpx, with no free_only check, no budget.record, and no openrouter_max_concurrency gate. The adapter's own vision path documents the opposite posture: llm.py:2757-2762 refuses to 'silently bill the paid default' under free_only when no vision_model is configured, and llm.py:2744-2756 treats an explicitly configured vision_model as the only spend opt-in.
win_rate_impact: With llm_backend=openrouter + the default free_only=1 and the game checks default-on, every game build fires multiple unmetered paid vision calls (judge + up to 2 click-grounding rounds with retries) that per_build_usd_cap/daily_usd_cap never see — a cost-guard bypass that erodes exactly the budget the operator bounded builds with, and contradicts the free_only contract two settings docstrings promise.
fix: In _make_openrouter_vision_fn, return None (soft-skip — the gates' skipped contract already handles it) when free_only is set and settings.vision_model is empty, mirroring llm.py:2757-2762; when it does run, record the spend to the budget ledger or at minimum log a per-call spend warning.

title: has_any_llm ignores the openrouter_enabled kill-switch
evidence: settings.py:741-751 returns bool(self.openrouter_api_key) — openrouter_enabled (settings.py:156-160, the documented dashboard-disconnect persistence, .env.example:76-78) is not consulted, even though every key-resolution site refuses the key when it is False (llm.py:303). With SKYN3T_OPENROUTER_ENABLED=0 and a key still in .env/env, /api/status policy.has_any_llm (deps.py:487) and the health fallback (health.py:252-257: 'provider key configured' → Status.OK) report a consumable LLM while generation resolves to the offline stub.
win_rate_impact: The M6 bug class ('status claims LLM availability while generation stays on stub') reintroduced through the enable flag: an operator or the autonomy loop sees green health and launches builds that run on the stub, each one burning a build slot and failing at the scaffold_stub gate — wasted attempts that drag the measured win rate down until someone notices the disconnect flag.
fix: Change has_any_llm to: return bool(self.openrouter_api_key) and bool(self.openrouter_enabled).

title: STALE_BASE deletes a fully verified candidate's worktree and branch when main advances mid-verify
evidence: candidate_engine.py:664-673 — after all verification gates pass, any advance of main since before_sha sets STALE_BASE, which is in _FAILED_CANDIDATE_STATUSES (:209-218). _finish (:797-821) then fails the preserve test (production policy sets preserve_failed_worktrees=False, candidate_service.py:465) and runs cleanup_candidate, which force-removes the worktree and deletes the candidate branch (:762-793), making the verified commit unreachable. This happens even when auto_merge is False and the candidate would only ever have been READY for later manual merge.
win_rate_impact: In an actively developed repo (this one has frequent commits and a large in-flight fix pass), any candidate whose 30-60 minute verify window overlaps one user commit is destroyed after paying full authoring + verification cost — ruff, full pytest, npm ci/test/build all passed and the result is discarded with no retry. Improvements that would raise the build win rate never land, and the budget spent proving them is pure loss.
fix: Treat STALE_BASE like READY for retention: remove it from the statuses that trigger cleanup (or preserve worktree+branch when status is STALE_BASE and all verification passed), so a verified-but-stale candidate can be rebased/merged instead of deleted.

title: Liveness reconciliation blanket-upgrades any no_go to go without checking the no_go's cause
evidence: runner.py:1829-1840: when `visual_self_heal_gate` is in manifest.extra and liveness looks perfect (proof.passed, 0 dead routes, visual_health >= 1.0), the code pops the gate and runs `if verdict == 'no_go': verdict = 'go'` unconditionally. But under lab posture the visual_self_heal finding never blocked (release-only, gate_posture.py:85; recorded via _gate_outcome at runner.py:6006-6010), so a no_go at this point is from a DIFFERENT cause — the reviewer/rescore AND-combine (5695), or in release posture substance/intent/scaffold_stub/code_degraded findings — and all of them get silently overridden to 'go'. The gate_findings ledger still shows a blocked finding while the manifest ships verdict=go.
win_rate_impact: Broken or brief-ignoring builds are counted as wins whenever visual self-heal is enabled and the rendered pages look healthy: a hollow-but-pretty scaffold that the reviewer or the substance/intent gates rejected ships as 'go'. This corrupts the win-rate signal itself and trains the lessons/learning loop on failures graded as successes (helpful = verdict=='go', runner.py:6173).
fix: Capture the verdict value immediately before the visual_self_heal gate is applied (runner.py:6005) and, in the liveness reconciliation, restore that saved value instead of hard-coding 'go' — i.e. only undo the flip that visual_self_heal itself caused.

title: stage_debug hands the improver no build/test error text, so early repair attempts no-op
evidence: stage_debug.py:58: `gaps = list(proof.missing) + list(proof.syntax_errors)` — omits `proof.error_gaps()`, which the delivery fix loop deliberately feeds (runner.py:4219-4222, per commit 4c4f6fe 'Surface TypeScript build errors to the improver'). When the code stage's proof fails on a real npm build/test error with no missing-checklist or syntax entries, `improve([])` reaches CodeImproverAgent with empty gaps: `_targets_from_gaps([])` finds nothing and `_discover_targets_via_repo_map` gets no repo_map from `_improve_once`'s payload (runner.py:2797-2806), so files_improved=0, ran=False — after which debug_stage still runs one more full `proof_run` (install+build+tests, up to ~400s) before breaking (stage_debug.py:86-104). The gaps also skip the QA-FAIL contract every other repair path uses.
win_rate_impact: The most common real failure class (compile/build errors) gets zero repair at the earliest, cheapest point — the per-stage debug pass that exists precisely so 'a broken early stage doesn't poison everything downstream' — and instead wastes a no-op improver dispatch plus a redundant multi-minute proof per code stage. Repair is deferred to the post-merge fix loop, consuming its bounded budget (6 attempts/720s) and wall-clock that times out long builds.
fix: In `_run_check`, build gaps as `proof.error_gaps() or (list(proof.missing) + list(proof.syntax_errors))` (wrapped via `format_fix_feedback(..., stage='stage_debug', ...)`), and skip the re-proof when the improver reported no change (move the `if not ran: break` before the second `_run_check`).

title: detect_reward_hacking flags legitimate pytest.mark.skipif/xfail as gamed tests and vetoes the build
evidence: build_verifier.py:132-138: any test file containing the substring 'pytest.skip', '@pytest.mark.skip' (which also matches the common, legitimate `@pytest.mark.skipif(...)`), or 'xfail' ANYWHERE (even a comment) sets `suspicious=True`. build_verifier.py:221-224 then fails the stage verdict, and runner.py:1271-1275 blocks on `reward.get('suspicious')` explicitly WITHOUT the `proof_build_passed` override that stale build failures get — a passing authoritative proof cannot clear it.
win_rate_impact: A working app whose generated tests include one platform/optional-dep `skipif` guard is branded 'reward-hacking suspected': no_go under release posture, and under lab the verifier verdict/details poison the manifest and learning signals. False accusation of correct work — the exact misgrading class the operator's gate_posture docstring calls out.
fix: Only flag unconditional skips: match `pytest.skip(` / `@pytest.mark.skip` NOT followed by `if`, drop the bare 'xfail' substring (require `@pytest.mark.xfail` on a majority of tests), and require that flagged files be the MAJORITY of the suite before setting suspicious.

title: web_polish fails any UI build containing a single emoji glyph
evidence: web_polish_check.py:33 `_DECORATIVE_EMOJI_RE` spans U+1F000-U+1FAFF and U+2600-U+26FF; lines 71-72 add the issue on the FIRST match anywhere in markup, making `ok=False`. runner.py:1681-1689 records the gate and calls `_score_after_finding` (1217-1230), capping the score at 74 even when lab posture leaves the verdict go; `_shape_final_score` (runner.py:1577-1578) further caps go builds at 86; release posture flips no_go at cap 44.
win_rate_impact: Generated apps use emoji constantly (weather icons, todo checkmarks, game HUDs — often exactly what the brief asked for). One glyph turns a polished, working delivery into a 74-capped 'degraded' build (or a release no_go), systematically training the learning loop that correct deliveries are mediocre and consuming polish-repair attention on a non-defect.
fix: Drop the emoji check from the blocking `issues` list (move it to `warnings`), or require emoji to be the dominant visual signal (e.g. >N distinct glyphs AND no _STYLE_RE hits) before it counts as an issue.
